newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil turns around to close 25 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil turns around to close 25 cents higher.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed slightly higher, and dealers said the rally in gas oil was more to keep up with Brent crude than with U.S. heating oil.
IPE November gas oil closed 25 cents up at $222.75 a tonne after dipping to a low of $222 a tonne earlier on Thursday.
"There was some liquidation and some stops were triggered on the upside. Gas oil mirrored what heating oil was doing and Brent had an effect," a futures broker said.
"It rallied back and it wasn't going to go down. It is now supported by Brent much more than it has been," he added.
NYMEX crude and product futures showed early strength on Thursday and regained some ground lost yesterday after the Energy Information Administration published weekly stocks data.
IPE Brent crude also rallied in the mid-afternoon on a combination of political instability in Russia and U.S. data showing a fall in crude and distillate stocks last week.
Dec Brent gained 41 cents to $24.35 a barrel in the afternoon after touching a low of $23.72 in early trade.
It was up 16 cents at $24.10 a barrel at 1653 GMT.
"It's up because of two things -- the U.S. data and the Russian news," said a broker.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday sacked his security chief, Alexander Lebeb.
Russia is the world's third largest oil producer and a key supplier of crude to European markets.
The U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) latest weekly report confirmed the tight picture on heating oil markets as winter approaches, dealers said.
The DOE figures showed distillate stocks fell 900,000 barrels last week. Crude stocks were down 3.3 million barrels.
Brokers said Dec Brent could test resistance at $24.48 a barrel before the end of the session.
